title: Art Above All
subtitle: And now, the most anticipated performance.

items.text: Art Above All
Vienna People's Opera

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: ... The Field Agent Squad cannot make it this time. They have a more urgent mission.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: But the Vienna Branch already requested support from the army, even though we haven't told them what is happening. They are irritated by the blatant attack.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: We'd better use the power of the "era" now.
Hofmann clips a Laplace-issued communicator back on her waist.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Only one question remains. Is the source of this intel reliable, Marcus?

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Are Isolde and Heinrich really playing in the premiere of Tosca?
She questions her assistant, but her gaze is fixed on Kakania, who sits there idle in thought and action.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Yes. It may sound a bit absurd, but that is Ms. Kakania's inference ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: ... It is you who asked for cooperation. I've done what I can and told you everything I know.
She hangs her head, her voice uncharacteristically dispirited.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Unless the show is canceled, Isolde will show up. She is a perfectionist when it comes to her work.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: If she shows up, so will Heinrich.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Neither of them is under bounty. And the upper class loves her performance, so it's not hard for them to guarantee a show even in these troubled times.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I know her well. She will be there ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: ... If I know her as well as I think I do.
Kakania says nothing more, and her eyes fix on a curtain, locking into a trance.
The opera is about to begin. The audience pass through the aisles and take their seats on the soft chairs.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: ... Madam Hofmann, what mission is the Field Agent Squad dealing with?
Marcus speaks up, trying, in the manner of her books on conversation, to ease the momentary awkwardness.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Assassinations. There's been an outbreak in the Empire over the past three days. They are sent to guard the important people.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: We're out of manpower right now, so don't expect any backup.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: But don't worry. We don't need to capture or defeat the Manus. Just focus on the original ritual.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Put your own safety first. Understand, Marcus?
Marcus signals her understanding. Once again, she dives into her "read" on the interior of the Vienna People's Opera.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Hmm? The audience is bigger than the tickets sold.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I counted the seats in the balcony and gallery. There are still too many people in the main hall. Are they all staff of the Vienna branch?

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: No. This could be the doing of Manus Vindictae.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Haha.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: What are you laughing at?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: At you, Ms. Foundation. You have no idea where you are. This is Vienna, the city of music!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: And this is Isolde and Tosca! People are crazy about them!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I bet they would even stand outside the railings if standing tickets were sold ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: And when it reaches act three, they would fling themselves over the edge, crying "O Scarpia, avanti a Dio!"
Hofmann's brow hangs heavy with vigilance.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: I don't get what you're saying, but it sounds even worse than Manus Vindictae.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I-I collected information about this opera ...
Marcus hands off another stack of material to her mentor.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: "Rome, 1800. Painter Mario Cavaradossi and singer Tosca are two lovers ..."

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: "Cavaradossi has been arrested for helping the fugitive Cesare Angelotti, former consul to the Roman Republic."

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: "To save her lover, Tosca turns to Scarpia, the Chief of Police."

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: "Scarpia has coveted Tosca for a long time, so he proposes that Cavaradossi will be freed if Tosca gives herself to him."

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: "Tosca submits to him, but when he tries to embrace her, Tosca stabs him in the heart with a dagger ..."

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: For heaven's sake! How did you make that sound so boring?!
Kakania stands up, unable to bear the indignity any longer.
She reaches out, snatching the stack.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I don't think you should read the script ahead of time. It takes away all the surprises.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Just let the singer guide you and immerse yourself in this world ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Isolde is very good in guiding the audience. She's the best there is!
Kakania grips the script tightly, ready and willing to defend her beloved play.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: As a seancer, her incredible arcane skills allow her to act like the characters themselves on stage.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: She can do all kinds of voices, even those that seem physically impossible ... When she does this, she becomes a completely different person, taking us to a world beyond reality.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It'll feel like witnessing a miracle firsthand.
She realizes her behavior is, for the moment, quite grossly inappropriate.
Kakania slinks back down and removes her glasses, holding them in her hand.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: ... Sorry. I got a little excited.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: So this is how much I looked forward to this opera ...
She trembles as her hands reach up to grasp her forehead, her voice falling into a sob.
Marcus hesitates, but eventually reaches out, placing a hand on her shoulder.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I'm sorry. I know you still see her as a friend.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: No. I'm just thinking ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I thought I knew my friends and my kin, but really I had no idea what they were truly thinking, even with this mirror and all the psychological theories.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I am like Pandora who opened the box without knowing what was inside. Was it hope, or destruction?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: That sounds ... dark ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: But I also think ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: ... Perhaps we can never truly understand one another, but things won't get any better if I give up because of it.
Kakania shakes her head, rubs her eyes forcefully, then puts on her glasses once more.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I can not turn my back on this.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Don't worry about me, Ms. Marcus. Now that I'm here, I will fulfill my promise.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I will stop her.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: As for the doomsday you talked about ... I don't know what I can do about it, to be honest.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: All I know is, if I don't stop her today, every day of my life will feel like doomsday.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: No matter what happens from here, the show has begun.
The lights dim.
Just as she had scripted it.
The black-haired opera singer steps to the front of the stage.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Please, enjoy.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Even if the world ends tomorrow, we still have a show to enjoy.
TO BE CONTINUED…
